prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 4 columns and 4 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 13 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a colouring-book drawing: contours only, in one thin uniform black line on white, most of the panel left white. Draw only the people and the few large shapes of the place (walls, doors, windows, a bed, a car). People are simple storyboard figures: hair is one smooth outline of its shape, like a cap, empty inside, with no strands, curls or waves; a face has one short line each for the eyes, brows, nose and mouth, and no stubble, wrinkles or jaw lines; a fence is its posts and top rail, a tree its outline. No texture, mesh, bricks, leaves or fabric folds; no shading, grey or solid black: dark hair, clothes and cars are outlines left white inside. Thin black panel borders, plain white gutters. Location: Sebastian's apartment, living room, Night, warm lamplight indoors, city lights glowing through the window.
Image 1: the character sheet of Natalie (25), look S1
Image 2: the character sheet of Sebastian (30), look S2
Image 3: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 4: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 5: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 6: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 7: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Image 8: the blocking reference of this segment, the same place with its people in their places at the start; use it only for where each person is and which way they face, and keep each person on that seat or spot, on the same side of the room, in every panel until a shot moves them; do not copy its colours or light
Image 9: the prop agreement; use only structure, material, and color
Image 10: the prop bag; use only structure, material, and color
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image, by the shape of the hairstyle, the build and the outfit in outline only; never copy the photograph's detail. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Axis and camera side for the whole scene: the camera stays on the kitchenette side of the room, by the right wall, looking across toward the front door on the left wall. The back wall, with the floor-to-ceiling window and the white bedroom door, runs along one side, and the charcoal couch is seen in profile. Natalie stands in the open bedroom doorway on the back wall in her ivory bridal gown and veil, with her pale-blue bag over her shoulder, facing into the bedroom. Sebastian, in his tuxedo, stands on the window side of the round coffee table, facing the couch. There is one charcoal three-seat couch facing the window, with the arc floor lamp at its front-door end. One round oak coffee table stands in front of the couch, between the couch and the window, with one blank white sheet of paper and one blue pen on it. One round dining table with two chairs stands between the couch and the kitchenette, near the bedroom door, and a white pillow lies on the dining chair nearer the couch.
Panel 1: Wide shot, locked-off camera, eye-level, from the kitchenette side; bedroom door at frame right, couch in profile at frame center. Natalie stops in the bedroom doorway in her wedding gown and looks into the single bedroom. Sebastian stands on the window side of the coffee table, watching her.
Panel 2: Medium close-up, clean single on Natalie, eye-level, framed tight on her face and shoulders. Natalie turns her head from the bedroom toward Sebastian, her brows raised.
Panel 3: Medium shot, over-the-shoulder shot past Natalie's shoulder at the bedroom doorway, eye-level. Sebastian stands by the coffee table and tips his head toward the couch with a relaxed look.
Panel 4: Medium shot, locked-off, eye-level, on Natalie in the doorway. Natalie folds her arms across her bodice and lifts her chin.
Panel 5: Medium shot, slight low angle, slow push in on Sebastian at the coffee table. Sebastian picks up the blank sheet of paper and the blue pen from the coffee table and holds them out toward Natalie.
Panel 6: Wide shot, pan following Natalie from the bedroom doorway to the couch, eye-level. Natalie walks from the doorway to the couch, sets her bag on the floor at the kitchenette end, sits there, takes the paper and pen from Sebastian and leans over the coffee table. Sebastian stays on the window side of the table.
Panel 7: Close-up insert, high angle, on the sheet on the coffee table. Natalie's hand writes neat blue cursive on the sheet of paper.
Panel 8: Medium shot, over-the-shoulder shot past Natalie seated on the couch, low angle up at Sebastian. Sebastian slides his hands into his pockets and looks down at the paper.
Panel 9: Medium close-up, eye-level, on Natalie bent over the coffee table. Natalie keeps writing, then glances up at Sebastian with a firm look.
Panel 10: Medium shot, locked-off, eye-level, on Sebastian by the coffee table. Sebastian gives a small nod and a half smile.
Panel 11: Close-up, clean single on Natalie's face, eye-level. Natalie's pen stops on the paper, and she looks up at him searchingly.
Panel 12: Medium shot, low angle, slow push in on Sebastian. Sebastian leans one hand on the edge of the coffee table, steady and unbothered.
Panel 13: Medium shot, high angle over the coffee table, Sebastian's hand at the frame edge. Natalie writes one more line on the agreement and taps the pen on it.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering.
